name: Yusuf Ziegler

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. This is confidential. What is an ordinary day at the firm like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: The depot sends fuel slips in batches, and I can usually find the one duplicate before the client rings. I lead the team preparing its accounts and tax returns, check the exceptions, then sit with a junior to explain the mistake. I am 43, with a master’s degree and a chartered accountancy qualification; I like teaching a useful check, but late records turn evenings into deadline work.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is happening at home, and how do you use AI now?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Mara works at a library desk, and our children Ada and Milo are both school age. We have a mortgage, but my salary is low for a team lead, we have less than a month saved, and few accounting firms are nearby. I use AI tools now and then for meeting notes, checking the draft against my notebook before sharing it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The fuel slips from the depot would still need matching to the bank line. A small sorter would not change when our mortgage payment leaves the account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my team a tool can group routine slips if we can check the original image. I would still put a named reviewer on the tax return and the client call.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, even a quiet technology year leaves me worried. I lead the accounts team and know the work well, but my pay is low for that role, we have less than a month saved, and few firms nearby could replace this wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep checking the depot accounts and use the AI meeting-note tool I already try now and then, with client numbers removed. I would cancel a paid sports subscription and transfer its monthly cost into a separate mortgage buffer on each payday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the house, not about a small receipt sorter. A broken boiler would eat most of our cash.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much does the subscription cost?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It is eighteen a month, which is worth moving to the buffer while we still have my pay. I would keep the free radio coverage for the matches.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why use AI for notes but not returns?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can correct a meeting date before a note goes out, but a wrong return can cost a client money. I use the note tool sometimes and check it against my notebook.

say: I would allow **routine slip grouping** only with original images.
I would keep a **named reviewer** for every tax return.
think: My **low team-lead pay** and under-one-month reserve already threaten the mortgage.
Few local firms limit a quick **wage replacement**.
do: Keep checking **depot accounts** and occasional AI notes against originals.
Cancel the **sports subscription** and put eighteen monthly into mortgage cash.
feel: I feel **anxious** about household bills despite steady work.
S0.quote: A broken boiler would eat most of our cash.
fieldNote: His anxiety comes from **underpay and thin reserves**, even without radical AI.
He uses AI **occasionally** for notes while keeping client numbers out and returns under human review.

steps.text: Keep depot accounts and checked AI meeting notes under current review
Deposit freed eighteen monthly into mortgage buffer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Writing replies and checking accounts are the jobs my team does all day. I would ask what happens to our hours before celebrating a faster draft.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues to test the software on past depot returns with known errors and keep a human sign-off. I would ask management whether the unfilled trainee place is still in the budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think the firm could combine my team with another and cut my paid lead hours, even if I am one of the stronger accountants. My partner Mara works at a library desk, and her own screen work could also shrink; less than a month saved leaves no long wait.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would ask for a paid supervised session on the firm’s approved checker and take it only if the test report is sound. If my hours fall in the first year, I would apply for a posted senior accountant vacancy only with written pay, hours, and a start date that cover the mortgage and school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because both household wages could be touched, but I can still ask for evidence. I am not planning to resign over a prediction.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if there is no paid session?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my current client files and use the professional body’s free examples while my salary continues. I would not feed a live return into an unfamiliar tool.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What about the trainee place?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The last trainee left in September and has not been replaced. I would ask for the actual vacancy budget, not tell the young applicants to wait for nothing.

say: I would ask for a **known-error test** and human sign-off.
I would ask whether the **trainee vacancy** is still funded.
think: My own **lead hours** could be cut despite strong skills.
Mara’s library-screen hours could shrink too, exposing **both incomes**.
do: Take **paid supervised checker training** only after a sound test report.
Use **free examples** while keeping current pay if no session is offered.
Seek **posted senior work** after hour cuts only with written mortgage pay, pickup-compatible hours and confirmed start.
S1.quote: I would ask for the actual vacancy budget, not tell the young applicants to wait for nothing.
fieldNote: He is a skilled lead yet fears **merged teams** and lost paid hours.
His AI learning is **conditional on paid supervision** and a sound test, with free study while employed if refused.

steps.text: Take paid supervised checker session after sound test; otherwise study free examples while employed
Take posted senior job after hour cuts only with written mortgage pay, pickup-fitting hours and start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Two years is shorter than a mortgage fix. Robots arriving around 2031 would not delay the accounting and library screens hit in 2028.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the firm to name who signs a return when AGI does the checking in 2028. I would tell Mara that robots around 2031 are later, while both our desk jobs face the first date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect my account-review post to go, and Mara’s library desk may lose hours too. Our savings would not cover even one month of mortgage and school costs without both wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would cancel the planned summer trip and put its monthly budget into emergency cash. If my accounting pay stops in the first year after 2028, I would apply for posted paid warehouse shelf-count and loading shifts only with written wages, shifts, and a start date covering the mortgage and school pickup; I would keep my present salary only while the firm still employs me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect a pay loss and cannot fund a long search. Paid shelf-count shifts may buy time before robots reach hands-on work, not solve the future.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Mara change her library work now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Mara would ask about paid hours at the library and keep those wages while they last. We cannot count on a second job until someone offers actual shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use family help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My father Tomas could collect the children for a month if a real new shift starts before Mara finishes work. I would ask only when a written job offer names those hours.

say: I would demand a **named return signer** in 2028.
I would say **2031 robots** do not delay the desk shock.
think: I expect my **review post** to disappear.
Mara’s library hours may also fall, while our **tiny reserve** cannot carry the mortgage.
do: Cancel the **summer trip** and deposit its monthly cost into emergency cash.
Take **paid shelf-count shifts** after job loss only with written mortgage-covering wages and school-compatible hours.
Ask my **father for pickup** only if a written shift clashes with Mara’s work.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by likely loss of pay and a tiny buffer.
S2.quote: Paid shelf-count shifts may buy time before robots reach hands-on work, not solve the future.
fieldNote: His possible warehouse bridge is **hands-on work** until later robots, not a shelter for accounting work.
Family pickup depends on a **written new shift**; he does not assume salary continues after dismissal.

steps.text: Deposit the planned monthly trip cost into emergency cash
After 2028 layoff, take posted paid loading shifts with written mortgage-covering wage, school-compatible hours, start date
Ask father Tomas for month-long pickup only if signed job shifts conflict with Mara’s hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years would let us see the staffing cuts before they happen. I could learn a different part of tax work while still drawing this wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues the firm should fund real client representation and post vacancies before 2031. AGI reaches our accounts desks then, while robots reach hands-on tasks around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still think the review post could vanish, but five years gives me time to build a record of solving disputed tax notices. Mara’s library work may also change, so I cannot spend our tiny buffer on a course gamble.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would enrol in the professional body’s notice-response module only if the firm pays its fee and gives paid study time, then work through one client objection quarterly if my manager Ren assigns supervised hours. I would move eighteen from each monthly wage into mortgage cash; in the first year after 2031 I would take a posted representation job only with written wage, hours, and a start date covering the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the eventual cut, but I can plan around real cases. I would keep the current salary while the firm still has work for me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Ren will not fund the module?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would read the free professional case notes while keeping my present returns and pay. I would not put the mortgage buffer toward a certificate with no role promised.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move before 2031?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only for a posted opening with a signed wage and start date that cover our fixed costs. There are few firms nearby, so I would not resign for a conversation.

say: I would seek **funded client representation** before 2031.
I would separate **2031 desk work** from later 2034 robots.
think: My **review post** could disappear when AGI reaches accounting desks in 2031.
Mara’s library role may also change, so our **thin cash** needs protection.
do: Complete a **funded notice module** on paid time; study free cases while employed if refused.
Practise **supervised client objections** quarterly only if Ren assigns paid hours.
Take **posted representation work** after 2031 only with written mortgage-covering terms.
feel: I feel **anxious** about two exposed wages.
S3.quote: I would not resign for a conversation.
fieldNote: He needs **funded fees** and paid study time before enrolling in a module.
His second route depends on **supervised paid objections** and a posted mortgage-covering vacancy, not a certificate alone.

steps.text: Complete employer-funded notice module with paid study; otherwise study free cases while retaining current returns/pay
Transfer eighteen monthly from salary into mortgage cash
After 2031, take posted representation job only with written mortgage-covering wage, hours and start date
Practise one supervised client objection quarterly only if Ren assigns paid hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years would get our children through more school years. I could build a reserve without leaving a paid job early.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the firm has time to keep junior learning and named sign-off before AGI reaches accounting desks in 2036. Robots around 2039 are a later change for hands-on jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect routine return fees to fall, and Mara’s library desk could also change in 2036. Our under-one-month reserve and low pay worry me now, even though the shock is ten years away.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep reviewing current depot returns and transfer eighteen from monthly pay into mortgage cash until we have three months of expenses. I would take supervised client objections only if Ren assigns paid time; if my lead post contracts in the first year after 2036, I would take a posted representation role only with written wages, hours, and a start date covering the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about this year’s bills, although the later desk change gives me time. I cannot pay the mortgage with a plan that starts in ten years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask for a raise now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show Ren the corrections my team caught and request a salary review this January. I would keep the present work while that decision is pending, because local alternatives are few.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my children Ada and Milo that I want them to learn how to check a claim, not only type an answer. I would not ask them to worry about our loan.

say: I would support **junior learning** and named sign-off before 2036.
I would say **2039 robots** do not delay accounting desk risk.
think: Routine return **fees** may fall after AGI reaches the accounts desk in 2036.
Our **thin reserve** and low pay threaten the mortgage even today.
do: Keep **depot returns** and assigned paid objections; request January 2027 salary review using team corrections.

Take **posted representation work** after a 2036 cut only with written mortgage-covering terms.
feel: I feel **anxious** about today’s household bills.
S4.quote: I cannot pay the mortgage with a plan that starts in ten years.
fieldNote: His baseline **thin buffer** keeps the slow AGI scenario from feeling safe.

If post contracts after 2036, take representation job with written mortgage-covering wage, hours and start date

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because both our screen-based wages could shrink before I find a signed new job. Funded notice-response training, a real vacancy with mortgage-covering pay, and temporary income support after a layoff would help. I would keep earning here only while the firm still has my post.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask how a junior learns when the first check is silent software. My best corrections began as someone explaining a mistake at my desk. I want that teaching time written into the job.

headlineQuote: My best corrections began as someone explaining a mistake at my desk.
portrait: Yusuf is a **43-year-old** team lead with a master’s degree and chartered qualification who checks depot returns.
He has **low pay**, under a month saved, a library-worker partner, two school-age children, and a mortgage.
He uses **AI occasionally** for checked meeting notes and lives near few accounting firms.
The **2028** desk shock threatens both household wages; temporary warehouse work needs posted shifts.
Longer warning allows **funded notice training** and new monthly deposits while the firm still pays him.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could cut both screen-work wages before he finds a signed mortgage-covering job.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **funded training**, a posted paid vacancy, and temporary income support after a layoff.
